# 般若波羅蜜多心經還源述

**ID:** T2746

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle anonymous Tang-era Heart Sūtra commentary preserved among the Dūnhuáng manuscripts and admitted into the Taishō canon as T2746 (Vol. 85 — the Dūnhuáng-materials volume). The Taishō head-note "[cf. No. 251]" cross-references the Xuánzàng short-recension parent text ([KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128)). One fascicle, anonymous.

The genre marker — *huányuán shù* "returning-to-the-source exposition" — suggests an integrated commentarial method that traces each Heart Sūtra phrase back to its doctrinal source-context within the larger Buddhist scriptural and contemplative tradition.

**Abstract**

T2746 is one of the small group of Tang-era Heart Sūtra commentaries preserved exclusively through Dūnhuáng manuscripts — paralleling [法成](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%88%90) Fǎchéng's T255 ([KR6c0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0132), which is a translation rather than a commentary), and a small number of other Dūnhuáng-only Heart Sūtra commentary fragments in the Stein and Pelliot collections.

Doctrinally the work belongs to the mature Tang Yogācāra-Madhyamaka synthesis tradition: the *four-truths* analytic, the careful *zhēnsú èrdì* (true-conventional two truths) treatment, the *sìyùn děng wúfēi yǒu* analysis. This places the work within the Cí'ēn-school ([窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) Kuíjī's lineage) doctrinal mainstream of the late-7th and 8th centuries, although it is too brief to be assigned to any specific named author.

The closing colophon material — the *[玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) Xuánzàng numinous-response* legend, the *five-hundred recitations purification ritual*, the *ninety-five heresies* protection promise — places the work in the Tang Heart Sūtra cultic-devotional tradition that grew up around Xuánzàng's translation and was elaborated through the *Hsüan-tsang miracle stories* recorded in the *Dà Táng Cí'ēnsì sānzàng fǎshī zhuàn* 大唐慈恩寺三藏法師傳 and elsewhere.

For the wider history of Heart Sūtra commentary, T2746 is a primary witness to the popular-devotional Tang Heart Sūtra reception that flourished alongside the elite scholastic commentaries ([窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) Kuíjī's T1710, [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) Wǒnch'ǔk's T1711, [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) Fǎzàng's T1712).

Composition date: no internal dating; provenance is the Dūnhuáng caves, sealed c. early 11th century. The bracket *notBefore* 700 (giving the text time to develop after [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) Xuánzàng's death in 664) / *notAfter* 900 (well within the Dūnhuáng cave-deposit horizon) is conservative; the work most likely belongs to the 8th or early-9th century.
